stumbles.quote: The two judges labelled 58 of those 63 as legitimate prose: the cells held numbers and labels, not sentences.
stumbles.why: "The two judges" are never introduced. The sentence also contradicts itself: cells holding numbers and labels, not sentences, are not "legitimate prose". The intended label is probably "false positives" or "not prose".

stumbles.quote: `--skip-quoted` already blanks table cells, but it also blanks blockquotes and italics.
stumbles.why: The flag is never defined, so I can't tell whether it is an existing flag or what it does. If it already blanks tables, the need for the new flag is unclear until the last sentence.

stumbles.quote: It is meant for drafts that quote bad prose in italics on purpose and still need their tables skipped.
stumbles.why: This is the only reason given for the flag. It doesn't connect to the 63-hit table-cell evidence, which has nothing to do with italics.

stumbles.quote: a scan of 41 published posts produced 300 lint hits
stumbles.why: The text doesn't say what the linter looks for or what a "hit" is. It also doesn't say how 58 of 63 false hits supports the flag.

stumbles.quote: With the flag set, the linter skips Markdown table rows and still scans the rest of the draft.
stumbles.why: "Draft" and "the declauding skill" are used without explanation. It's unclear what the linter is checking for.

point: The PR adds a `--skip-tables` flag that blanks Markdown table lines before linting, so line numbers stay correct, because most table-cell lint hits were false positives. The rationale is muddled by undefined judges and an unexplained `--skip-quoted`.
